question.text: 'Hariyali Foundation' implements watershed management and solar projects in drought-prone regions. Per Ch 1.5.3, which risk category BEST fits the dependence of programme outcomes on climatic conditions?

answer.text: Strategic Risk — programme design is funder-driven
Regulatory Risk — changes in CSR Schedule VII
Environmental Risk — climate change and global warming affecting outcomes and impact

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 1.5.3 (vi), Environmental Risk covers solar projects, watershed management, and agricultural interventions whose outcomes depend on climatic and environmental conditions. Climate change and global warming directly affect these interventions. The Trap: Option A is about strategy formulation, Option B about digital tools, Option C about regulatory changes — all valid risk categories but not the best fit for climate-dependence. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to Ch 6 (Frameworks — environmental SAS standards) and Ch 8 (Case Studies). For SAS-500 environmental engagements, risk characterisation is a required scoping step. Assessor's Pro-Tip: For SAS-500 engagements, require the SE to present a climate-risk register (rainfall variance, seasonal solar irradiance, groundwater trends). Without this, your assumption-testing on project outputs lacks baseline — escalate in scoping.
